items.headline: Simplifying agent access while keeping organizations in control: MCP servers, CLI, standardized usage tiers, and admin policies
items.summary: As AI agents transform how people work, we want to make it simple for developers to build agentic workflows while keeping organizations in control of their data in Google Workspace. We are making Workspace Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and the official Workspace CLI generally available alongside standardized usage tiers to simplify how developers build and scale agents, paired with a new Workspace AI Tools Addendum and expanded enterprise controls over AI agents. Google also introduced a new Workspace AI Tools Addendum and expanded enterprise controls over AI agents.
Developers can connect AI agents to Workspace without custom integration code, while organizations keep control of their data.

items.headline: DigitalOcean Insights is now generally available: Unified observability across every layer of your stack
items.summary: Observability is critical for running software in production. It helps teams understand whether a service is healthy, why a request slowed down, and what changed before an incident began. Answering those questions draws on more than one signal. Metrics show that behavior has changed, logs record what happened, and traces show where along a request’s path it happened. These signals are most useful when you can move from one to the next without losing context. As a stack grows to span clusters, databases, and agents, a unified view across every layer allows a team to keep pace with the system it operates. DigitalOcean Insights gives you a unified observability stack built into the DigitalOcean
lines: DigitalOcean Insights is now generally available as a unified observability stack built into DigitalOcean.
The product brings together metrics, logs, and traces so users can move between signals without losing context.
It is aimed at stacks that span clusters, databases, and agents.

items.headline: CVE-2026-123633 Portfolio Status: Impact of NGINX Vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123007) on Palo Alto Networks Products (Severity: CRITICAL)

lines: Palo Alto Networks published an advisory on two Critical severity NGINX vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, and their impact on its products.

items.headline: Hackers Exploit Two GeoServer Flaws as Researchers Warn of Unauthenticated RCE Chains
items.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting two newly patched security flaws in GeoServer, according to watchTowr. The vulnerabilities in question are CVE-2026-120705 and CVE-2026-129243, details of which are below - CVE-2026-120705 (CVSS score: 8.6) - An arbitrary file read vulnerability that could enable an attacker to access local text files readable by the GeoServer process or fetch
lines: Reported by The Hacker News: Threat actors are actively exploiting two newly patched security flaws in GeoServer, according to watchTowr.
The flaws are CVE-2026-120705, with a CVSS score of 8.6 and an arbitrary file read vulnerability, and CVE-2026-129243.
Researchers also warn of unauthenticated remote code execution chains.
IT teams running GeoServer should confirm these patches are applied and check their systems for signs of exploitation.
